intro_what: An OpenAI-compatible security gateway for AI agents. Tool results, fetched pages, MCP payloads and RAG chunks pass through spanguard before the agent reads them; a 135M-parameter multilingual span model plus validated rules find prompt-injection text inside the data and replace each span with [stripped], while orders, totals, names and JSON structure survive untouched.
intro_alternative: The strongest open binary guard on the same set (horizon injection-guard base, strip-all semantics) reaches 6.2% escape only by over-stripping 59.0% of benign characters — the agent loses most of what it was reading; protectai deberta-v3 is worse than spanguard on BOTH axes (35.4% escape, 71.8% over-strip); a 0.5B LLM asked to flag its own injections misses 91.7%
intro_measured: Committed run records per system and set (eval/results/), fictional data only, an external public set for generalization, per-attack-family heatmaps, CPU latency measured where each system ran, and a cost ledger. Rerun everything with `make eval` + the Kaggle kernels in training/train/.
latency_note: p50 latency per document, model-only path, measured where each system ran: rules ≈0.2 ms, the 135M span model adds tens of ms on CPU (2 threads, recovery build); the LLM self-detect column includes local generation time
cost_note: LLM-based guarding pays per token; local guards pay $0 per document — computed from recorded token usage at Baseten list prices
